chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man intends to travel and sets out; when does he shorten his prayer?' He said, 'When the houses become hidden from him.' I said: 'The man intends to travel and sets out when the sun sets.' He said, 'When you set out, pray two rak'ahs.'
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler begin shortening their prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise moment the ruling of *qasr* (shortening prayer) takes effect, with the primary criterion being the visibility of the city's dwellings (*tawari min al-buyut*), a standard definition of leaving the urban boundary in Shia jurisprudence. It also offers a practical alternative for those departing at sunset, instructing them to perform two rak'ahs immediately upon exiting, reflecting the flexibility within the Imami school regarding travel timing and prayer consolidation.
